findings.title: The relative phrase enters the object

findings.title: Coercion as loss of footing
findings.claim: The attributed reading moves from wanted expulsion to a purpose that makes a settled people movable and targets them for removal.
findings.mechanism: Arada carries purpose, yastafizzahum supplies destabilizing force, and min al-ard names the ground from which movement is intended; their contact turns expulsion into ungrounding.
findings.reader_payoff: The plan acts on people's footing and settled condition, not only their location.
findings.containment: This is an attributed HFT interpretation. The grounded-population image is a relation among intent, destabilization, and land, not a claim that al-ard means lingering or that departure occurred.

epistemic.reason: The HFT identity is legacy-unbound and supplies no morphology; its indices and roots agree with QAC occurrences, and the cited branches have registry records.

findings.title: The aggressor loses the footing he would unsettle
findings.claim: The attributed reading reverses attempted displacement: the maker of instability is himself submerged and deprived of footing.
findings.mechanism: Yastafizzahum carries destabilizing force, al-ard supplies the surface from which removal is planned, and aghraqnahu supplies submersion; their contact turns the outward program into engulfing descent.
findings.reader_payoff: The response answers planned loss of others' footing with the aggressor's own loss of ground and spatial control.
findings.containment: Before: attempted expulsion followed by drowning. After: the destabilizer becomes groundless. This focus-local image claims no wider fate beyond the people named.

epistemic.reason: The HFT source is legacy-unbound and supplies no morphology; its indices and roots match QAC focus occurrences and its branch facets are in the registry.

findings.title: A bounded land-body analogy
findings.claim: As an exploratory material analogy, coercive agitation irritates a land-body like a wound, and attempted discharge becomes inundation that overtakes its agent.
findings.mechanism: Yastafizzahum supplies unsettling action, al-ard the ground-body image, and aghraqnahu drowning; their cross-root contact links wet discharge, corrupted ground, and engulfing water.
findings.reader_payoff: A coercive effort to disturb the land-body culminates in an inundation that overtakes its would-be agent.
findings.containment: This is the HFT's branch-distant political-pathology analogy, not a claim that the words lexically mean wound, ulcer, or water-saturated land. The before reading remains territorial coercion followed by drowning.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates and roots match QAC focus words, but the multi-step wound chain is an attributed analogy from a legacy-unbound source.
